close_reason: Not landed; folded into fz-sc8.176. Suite census (849 fixtures): fz-lr6 alone costs +510 applied runs; the untyped join costs +2,987 with lr6 and adds churn (shift wakes 2,859 -> 3,660, withdrawn activations 1 -> 35, InputDemand revisions 33 -> 297) because it answers before an implementation lands; joining after every provider is defined costs +30,526 (not proportional). The precise form is a returned axis per receiver type, which needs per-key demand: fz-sc8.176 item 4.
description:
keying.rs visit_protocol_callback marked every non-receiver input of a protocol callback returned Whole, because an implementation may hand an accumulator back and asking the implementations would make the answer move as implementations land. Sound, but conservative: Enumerable.reduce_while/3's reducer is marked returned though no implementation in lib returns it. Under fz-lr6 (a returned callable keeps its identity), every Enum wrapper's reducer then keys per lambda: 00420 +124 jobs, 00571 188 -> 199 executables.

Change (option 2, approved): the callback hands each input to the same input of every implementation ProtocolDispatch names for it, on an EdgeReach::Implementation forward edge. The returned axis joins across those edges; the dispatch axis does not (an implementation's questions are asked at its own key). Enumerable.reduce_while/3 publishes returned [Ignore, Whole, Ignore]: the accumulator, not the reducer.

Measured (experiment tree, three variants x lr6 on/off):
- join (this change): under fz-lr6 every one of lr6's seven rises vanishes (00571 stays 188). Alone it costs 00420 2,529 -> 2,569 jobs (+29 DeriveInputDemand, +4 DeriveStaticCallees, +7 AnalyzeActivation; executable facts unchanged at 246); take-derivation (75,244,8) -> (96,354,9); 00181 213 -> 216; 00567 shifts (7,18) -> (11,25); distiller drive 47,688 -> 47,488.
- The cost is revision: Enumerable.List lands after the callback's first answer, so the callback and its forwarders (Enum.reduce_while/3, Enum.all?/1) are revised once. The 'published once' rule is retired; revisions only widen.
- Waiting for every provider before joining (no revisions) loads implementations the program never reaches: 00181 formula work 213 -> 424, take-derivation 75 -> 165 runs. Rejected.

Follow-on, not in this change: state the returned axis per receiver type at the call, the way resolve_protocol_call already demands only the providers the receiver overlaps. That is precise, stable (no revisions) and proportional, but InputDemand is one answer per function today, so it belongs with fz-sc8.176's per-key demand.

Acceptance: 00420 under fz-lr6 returns to this change's own count; no fixture changes output; pins attributed.
title: A protocol callback states which inputs its implementations return, not every input
